id: title:dmarchuk:retry an apns send when apple rejects the token of a key that works

review.posthog_relevance: Push notification delivery reliability and recovery handling for Apple Push Notification service (APNs) within PostHog's backend, specifically regarding token rejection and rate-limiting recovery.
review.reason: This chunk represents a substantive, bounded improvement to the push notification delivery subsystem. The observed changes include adding assertions for HTTP headers in mocked responses and, more critically, adding tests for recovery behaviors: rescheduling sends after token rejection and carrying acceptance evidence across pods during 429 (rate-limit) responses. review.uncertainty: While the implementation and relevant checks are visible, the actual runtime behavior and complete implementation of the recovery logic are not shown in this chunk, which is dominated by test assertions. The tier is assigned based on the demonstrated intent and structure of the recovery and compatibility checks, not on unverified production outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs are present. No score is assigned; tier selection requires a score and an explanation, not just observations.

observations.behavior: Adds a `headers` parameter to the mocked APNs response in the test, including it in the returned object.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows tests to assert or inspect HTTP headers returned by APNs, supporting assertions about header-based behavior or compatibility with real APNs responses.

observations.behavior: Adds a new test asserting that when APNs rejects a token but the key delivered recently, the send is rescheduled rather than failing, and that this rescheduling carries the evidence of acceptance across pods.
